content: The International Micronutrient Malnutrition Prevention and Control Program (IMMPaCt) provides financial support to the secretariat of the Food Fortification Initiative. This initiative focuses on fortifying wheat flour with essential vitamins and minerals. Leaders from the relevant division also participate as observers on the Executive Management Team of the Food Fortification Initiative. During the second guideline development group meeting, Dr. Jefferds actively participated in decision-making processes. She was required to verbally disclose any potential conflicts of interest to the other participants. The World Health Organization (WHO) mandates a conflict-of-interest analysis whenever it relies on independent expert advice to make decisions or provide recommendations to Member States or stakeholders. A conflict of interest is defined as any declared interest that could influence or be perceived to influence an expert’s objectivity and independence in advising WHO. WHO’s conflict-of-interest policies aim to prevent situations that could compromise the integrity of the expert, the committee, the activity, or WHO as a whole. The scope of the inquiry includes any interest that could reasonably be perceived to affect the expert’s functions. Dr. Lynette Neufeld disclosed that her employer, the Global Alliance for Improved Nutrition, supports food fortification programs. She has conducted research and authored publications in the field of food fortification. For the second guideline development group meeting, Dr. Neufeld declared that her organization had received funding for research and programming related to food fortification. However, she was not directly leading any of these initiatives, despite her publications in the field. She fully participated in decision-making during the meeting and disclosed her personal interests and her employer’s involvement in food fortification projects. Ms. Carol Tom declared her employment with the United States Agency for International Development (USAID)/A2Z on a project related to child blindness and micronutrients. She also serves as a consultant for the East, Central, and Southern African Health Community (ECSA-HC) on food fortification. It was determined that her employment did not present any conflict of interest for the meeting, as USAID is a U.S. government agency and ECSA-HC is a regional association of health ministries. She was allowed to fully participate in the deliberations and decision-making for the guideline. The systematic review teams declared no conflicts of interest and did not participate in the deliberations or decision-making processes. The WHO Secretariat will continue to monitor research developments in wheat flour fortification, particularly in areas where evidence is limited or of very low quality. If the guideline requires an update or if concerns arise regarding its validity, the Department of Nutrition and Food Safety, in collaboration with other WHO departments or programs, will coordinate the update process following the formal procedures outlined in the WHO handbook for guideline development.
